title: Typing Children and Special Props
description: Learn to type ReactNode children, refs, keys, and other special React props.

data.text: React components often receive special props that are not declared in your interface. Understanding how to type children, refs, and keys keeps your components fully type-safe while staying idiomatic.

data.title: Children with ReactNode
Prefer ReactNode
data.text: ReactNode is the most permissive and common choice for children. It accepts almost anything React can render, which matches how JSX actually works.

data.title: Ref Forwarding

data.text: Special Props You Should NOT Type
React manages some props automatically. You should not declare them in your interface, and TypeScript will not let you access them inside the component.

terms.definition: A special prop used by React to identify elements in a list. It is not accessible inside the component.
A special prop that gives access to the underlying DOM node or component instance.
Content placed between the opening and closing tags of a component.

data.text: When a component should accept any HTML attribute, extend React.HTMLAttributes instead of listing props manually.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Do not declare key or ref in interfaces
data.takeaway: Typing special props correctly keeps components flexible and type-safe.
